title: Walaeus' warning: it must not be used to make election depend on free choice, or to deny physical grace
source_text: XXX. Sed praecipue cavendum esse docet, nequis ista scientia abutatur vel ad decretum electionis a bono usu liberi Arbitrii hominis perpendendum, ut faciunt illi qui volunt, Deum priusquam hominem elegit, praevidisse quomodo, si haec aut illa gratia praeveniens & concomitans, in hoc aut illo ordine rerum, vel in hoc aut illo statu homini offerretur, ille per liberum arbitrium ei esset assensurus, aut non assensurus, adeo ut liberum arbitrium gratiam Dei eis determinet, non contra. Vel etiam ad negandam omnem Dei operationem efficacem in hominis convertendi voluntate, praeter moralem institutionem: quoniam, ut postea demonstraturum se confidit, Deus non tantum moraliter, sed etiam Physice agit in hominis voluntate, quando eum convertit.
pass_a_gloss: XXX. But he teaches that it must especially be guarded, lest anyone abuse that knowledge either for weighing the decree of election from the good use of man's free Choice, as those do who will, that God before he elected a man, foresaw how, if this or that preventing and concomitant grace, in this or that order of things, or in this or that state should be offered to man, he would by free choice assent to it, or not assent, so that free choice determines the grace of God for them, not the contrary. Or also for denying every efficacious operation of God in the will of man to be converted, besides moral instruction: because, as he trusts he will afterwards demonstrate, God acts not only morally, but also Physically in the will of man, when he converts him.
pass_b_english: But he teaches that we must take special care that no one misuses this knowledge. One misuse is to weigh the decree of election by the good use of a person's free choice. Those who do this hold that God, before electing someone, foresaw how that person would respond if this or that preventing and accompanying grace were offered him in this or that order of things or state. He foresaw whether the person would assent to it by free choice or not. On this view free choice determines God's grace for them, not the other way round.

The other misuse is to deny that God works efficaciously in the will of the person being converted, beyond moral instruction. As Walaeus expects to show later, God acts in a person's will not only morally but also physically when he converts him.
